summary.title_hr: STEPHAN LUPINO – Najljepše žene na svijetu su susjede – PODCAST ČUŠPAJZ #168
summary.abstract_hr: U 168. epizodi Podcasta Čušpajz gost je fotograf i umjetnik Stephan Lupino. Govori o svom putu iz Rima preko Londona do New Yorka, o suradnji s fotografkinjom Deborah Turbovel te o New Yorku i Studiju 54 krajem sedamdesetih i početkom osamdesetih. Kritički se osvrće na današnju modu, influencere, društvene mreže i umjetnu inteligenciju. Govori i o svom umjetničkom stilu lupinizmu, o povratku u Hrvatsku na početku rata te o hrvatskom mentalitetu. Zaključuje da se od fotografije danas ne može živjeti i mladima preporučuje da im ona bude hobi.
key_points: Lupino se nedavno vratio iz Pariza, gdje se snima dokumentarni film o Deborah Turbovel. Ona ga je prva fotografirala, a zahvaljujući njoj postao je fotograf i umjetnik. Paralelno se snima i dokumentarac o njegovu životu.

Prije New Yorka četiri je godine živio u Rimu kao učitelj karatea i tjelohranitelj, a zatim dvije godine u Londonu. Glumica Irena Papas nagovorila ga je da ode u New York, kamo je otišao s dva kofera u dobi od oko 24 ili 25 godina.

Navodi da je vrhunac Studija 54 bio 1977. – 1979. te da je on u New York stigao krajem 1979. i 1980., kada se klub već zatvarao. Kaže da oko 90 % ljudi koje je tada poznavao više nije živo zbog droge i alkohola.

Smatra da je nekadašnja elita bila originalnija, a da je današnja svijet 'copy-paste' i lova na lajkove. Manekenke su nekad bile 'kao bogovi', dok je danas moda izumrla, a fotografija se samo ponavlja i radi hommage na sedamdesete i osamdesete.
Lupinizam opisuje kao vlastiti stil koji spaja fotografiju, kiparstvo i život. Vjeruje da će se njegova vrijednost pokazati tek za dvadesetak ili tridesetak godina.
U Hrvatsku se vratio kad je počeo rat i kad je vidio Vukovar. Smatra da Hrvati žive tuđe živote, da su ljubomorni i skloni grupiranju radi profita te da talentirane mlade koče uhljebi.

Mladim fotografima savjetuje da se bave nečim drugim, primjerice keramikom ili električarskim zanatom, jer se od fotografije više ne može živjeti. Fotografija im, po njegovu mišljenju, treba biti hobi.
key_topics_en: life in new york in the eighties
key_points_en: Lupino recently returned from Paris, where a documentary film about Deborah Turbovel is being filmed. She was the first to photograph him, and thanks to her he became a photographer and artist. In parallel, a documentary about his life is also being filmed.

Before New York, he lived in Rome for four years as a karate teacher and bodyguard, and then for two years in London. Actress Irena Papas persuaded him to go to New York, where he went with two suitcases at the age of about 24 or 25.

He states that the peak of Studio 54 was 1977–1979 and that he arrived in New York in late 1979 and 1980, when the club was already closing. He says that about 90% of the people he knew then are no longer alive due to drugs and alcohol.

He believes that the elite of the past was more original, while today's is a world of 'copy-paste' and hunting for likes. Models once were 'like gods', while today fashion has died out, and photography only repeats itself and does an homage to the seventies and eighties.
He describes Lupinism as his own style that combines photography, sculpture, and life. He believes that its value will only become evident in twenty or thirty years.

He returned to Croatia when the war began and when he saw Vukovar. He believes that Croats live other people's lives, that they are jealous and prone to grouping together for profit, and that talented youth are held back by political freeloaders.

He advises young photographers to do something else, such as ceramics or the electrician's trade, because one can no longer make a living from photography. In his opinion, photography should be their hobby.
summary.title_en: STEPHAN LUPINO – The Most Beautiful Women in the World Are Next-Door Neighbors – PODCAST ČUŠPAJZ #168
summary.abstract_en: In the 168th episode of Podcast Čušpajz, the guest is photographer and artist Stephan Lupino. He talks about his journey from Rome through London to New York, about his collaboration with photographer Deborah Turbovel, and about New York and Studio 54 at the end of the seventies and the beginning of the eighties. He critically reflects on today's fashion, influencers, social networks, and artificial intelligence. He also speaks about his artistic style Lupinism, about returning to Croatia at the beginning of the war, and about the Croatian mentality. He concludes that one cannot make a living from photography today and recommends to young people that it be their hobby.
